newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks on Colombia port strike set for later today.
newsitem.headline: Talks on Colombia port strike set for later today.

text.p: Dock workers will meet with government officials and cargo handling operators at 1500 local/2000 GMT Tuesday in a bid to resolve the strike at Colombia's main Pacific coast port, a union leader said.

The port of Buenaventura, the shipment point for 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports and all its sugar exports, has been paralyzed for seven days. The port is estimated to be losing $500,000 for every day of the strike.
Nelson Amaya, regional head of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT) to which the dockers' union is affiliated, said the meeting had been moved from Bogota to Cali.
"Nobody believes the strike will be lifted today but there are good prospects for an agreement and hopefully we can sort this mess out soon," said Amaya.

A private coffee exporters association said 145,000 60-kg bags of private coffee exports were blocked in Buenaventura. About 160,000 60-kg bags of National Coffee Growers' Federation exports have been snarled in the action.
At least 27,000 tonnes of sugar exports have been paralyzed in the strike, according to port authorities.

The 3,000 dockers are looking for a wage hike and additional payments for social security, sickness and injury benefits. The average dock worker in Buenaventura earns less than $80 per month because of a "dirty price war" between operators that has pushed down cargo handling rates and ultimately whittled away wage levels, a port source said.
